name: Binary Bubble Sort Inversions
description: Define performing a bubble on an array $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_m$$$ to be performing the following action: For each integer $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \leq i \lt m$$$) in order , if $$$b_i \gt b_{i+1}$$$, swap $$$b_i$$$ and $$$b_{i+1}$$$. Define performing a reverse bubble on an array $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_m$$$ to be performing the following action: For each integer $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \leq i \lt m$$$) in reverse order , if $$$b_i \gt b_{i+1}$$$, swap $$$b_i$$$ and $$$b_{i+1}$$$. For example, if we perform a bubble on $$$[1, 1, 0]$$$, we would transform it as follows: $$$[\color{red}{1, 1}, 0] \to [1, \color{red}{1, 0}] \to [1, 0, 1]$$$. If we perform a reverse bubble on $$$[1, 1, 0]$$$, we would transform it as follows: $$$[1, \color{red}{1, 0}] \to[\color{red}{1, 0}, 1] \to [0, 1, 1]$$$. You are given an array $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ consisting of only 0 s and 1 s and a binary string$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$. You perform $$$n$$$ operations in order , where the $$$i$$$-th operation performs a bubble on $$$a$$$ if $$$s_i = \texttt{1}$$$ and performs a reverse bubble on $$$a$$$ if $$$s_i = \texttt{0}$$$. For each of the $$$n + 1$$$ states of $$$a$$$ — before any operations have been performed and after each operation — count the number of inversions$$$^{\text{†}}$$$ in $$$a$$$. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A binary string is a string that only contains 0 s and 1 s. $$$^{\text{†}}$$$An inversion in an array $$$c$$$ of length $$$m$$$ is a pair of indices $$$i, j$$$ such that $$$1 \leq i \lt j \leq m$$$ and $$$c_i \gt c_j$$$.
input_specification: The first line of each input contains $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 5 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of $$$a$$$ and $$$s$$$. The second line of each test case contains $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_i \leq 1$$$) — the array $$$a$$$. The third line of each test case contains $$$s$$$ ($$$s_i \in \{0, 1\}$$$, $$$|s| = n$$$$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$) — the binary string $$$s$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$$$$|c|$$$ denotes the length of a string $$$c$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output $$$n + 1$$$ space separated integers, the $$$i$$$-th integer denoting the number of inversions in $$$a$$$ after the first $$$i - 1$$$ operations have been performed.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
